OMEN · test 1

One hundred charts. Grade, entry, stop.

09:30–11:00, one-minute candles, PDH/PDL, PMH/PML and ORH/ORL drawn. Grade every chart S / A / C / X; on the ones you would trade, mark where you got in and where your stop was. Five parts of twenty. It saves as you go, and every control is a tap.

0 / 0saved

Select all the text in the box below and copy it (the box is editable, so ctrl/cmd+A then ctrl/cmd+C works even where the Copy button is blocked), then paste it into the chat. Download works too when the browser allows it.

How this is scored, before you start

You asked to match on 95% of the S calls. That fraction is only as readable as its denominator, so this test is sized around the denominator rather than the other way round.

100 cards. 45 of them are days the engine’s own S/A/C grader already calls S — that is the half of the denominator I know before you touch it. Every S you add from the other 55 cards grows it further, which only makes the target easier to read.

At a denominator of 45, one disagreement costs 2.2 points, so the target survives 2 of them: 43/45 = 95.6% passes, 42/45 = 93.3% fails. Cut this to the 60-card deck standard and the same mix carries about 27 S cards — one disagreement costs 3.7 points and the target survives only 1, so a single chart decides the result. That is why this is longer than the standard allows, and it is the only reason.

  • Sclean — nothing tripped
  • Aone downgrade
  • Ctwo downgrades (the floor)
  • Xno trade here at all. On the engine’s old ladder X meant “it should not have fired”. Here you are grading a chart, not an engine output, so X is simply your none: you would not have taken anything in this window.

Only the grade is required. Tap X and the card is finished in one tap. Entry, stop and setup appear only once you grade a chart tradeable.

Your answers cannot go anywhere

Every tap writes to this browser the moment you make it. Close the tab, lose the battery, come back next week — it is all still here, including the entry and the stop. The indicator at the top says saved each time it lands, and if your browser ever refuses to store it, that indicator turns red and says so. It does not fail quietly.

When you are done — or partway, it does not matter — hit Export, then Copy all, and paste it into the chat. The box is an ordinary editable text box, so ctrl/cmd+A then ctrl/cmd+C works even where the button is blocked. Download .jsonl works too where the browser allows it.

Not one of these 100 charts is a day you have judged before, in any file I hold — 758 already-judged symbol-days were removed from the pool before the draw, and no symbol-day appears on two cards.

or scroll back up — the bar follows you
